compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The reconcile-bridge-canary workflow carries ~200 lines of production logic in YAML run-blocks — staleness classification, two alert-ticket lifecycle state machines (heartbeat + binding-drift), each with find/open/comment/close steps. This is the highest-defect shell surface (449f: 7 recommendations), untestable and unlintable by ruff. The companion reconcile-bridge.yml push-back loop was ALSO a defect source (4c4f), but that loop's fix deliberately kept it in YAML under a verbatim-execution test — see Alternatives below.

## Alternatives / prior art
tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py (ticket 4c4f) established that CAS push loops on the hot tickets ref stay in workflow YAML and are tested VERBATIM (extracting them creates an untested-glue drift seam; the block contains zero ${{ }} expressions so the YAML itself is executable under test). This plan honors that decision: BOTH CAS push loops — reconcile-bridge.yml "Commit reconciler events back and push" (93L) and the canary's "Flush any unpushed ticket changes" (35L) — are OUT of scope and stay in YAML. What migrates is classification/alert-lifecycle logic, which differs from the push loops in kind: it has branchy decision logic (API-error vs zero-state vs stale; dedup-find vs open vs comment vs close), no git-ref CAS races, and it currently interleaves ${{ }} expressions with logic — exactly the shape that benefits from extraction + unit tests. The drift-seam risk the 4c4f rationale warns about is mitigated the same way the probe port (f1eb) mitigated it: an anti-rot unit test pins the thin YAML invocations (workflow parses, step invokes the canonical Python entry point with the expected env/args), and the extracted functions carry their own unit tests.

Deployment note: the f1eb executes-from-main trap does NOT apply here — gerrit-verify.yaml never runs the canary, and reconcile-bridge-canary.yml executes from main on schedule/workflow_dispatch only AFTER this change merges, so workflow edits and the new script deploy atomically; no transitional shim is needed.

The reconcile-bridge raw git write (the 93L commit-back loop) is NOT routed through the library write seam: it is workflow-only orchestration on a dedicated CI worktree, and the seam's own code warns a whole-index commit there races normal store writes. Instead, the raw-git-write lint child (d37e) allowlists the two verbatim-tested YAML loops as documented exceptions; this ticket records that contract in the migrated module's docstring.

## Approach
Strangler-fig on reconcile-bridge-canary.yml only: move the four logic families into one Python module invoked by thin YAML steps.
1. scripts/canary_bridge.py (new, single module, ~250-400 LOC): subcommands
   - check-heartbeat: GitHub API query (gh api via subprocess, injected runner seam) + classification {api-error->transient/no-alert, no-success-runs->stale(never), older-than-window->stale, fresh->ok}; emits GITHUB_OUTPUT keys (stale, last_run_ago, status_msg) exactly as today.
   - heartbeat-alert: the find/open/comment/close lifecycle against rebar CLI (find existing open alert by marker tag, open when stale+none, comment when still stale, close on recovery) — one function per transition, dedup pattern preserved. Error handling — PRESERVE each step's existing failure disposition (verified against the YAML), not a blanket rule: (a) alert-lifecycle WRITES (create/comment/transition close) have NO fallback in YAML today -> stay FAIL LOUD (non-zero exit -> red canary run; a silently swallowed alert-write failure would defeat the canary); (b) the dedup FINDs (`rebar list ... || echo ''`, YAML lines 218-219/341-342) deliberately degrade to empty -> the subcommand preserves fail-soft-to-not-found (treat CLI failure as 'no existing alert'); (c) check-binding-drift: `rebar bridge-fsck` exits 1 BY DESIGN when it finds drift (the signal the canary exists to detect; YAML line 316 `|| true`) -> the subcommand captures stdout regardless of exit code, parses JSON, and treats unparseable/empty output as empty drift data exactly as the YAML python block does today — exit 1 with valid JSON is DRIFT (alert path), never an error; unit tests cover each disposition: fsck-exit-1-with-drift-JSON -> drift reported; fsck-garbage-output -> empty drift; alert-write failure -> non-zero exit. DRY_RUN: the step-level `if: env.DRY_RUN == 'false'` gates stay in YAML, AND the subcommands re-check DRY_RUN from env and short-circuit all rebar writes when 'true' (defense in depth against a dropped `if:`).
   - check-binding-drift + binding-drift-alert: same two shapes for the second alert family.
2. Thin YAML: each replaced step becomes env + `python scripts/canary_bridge.py <subcommand>`; ${{ }} values pass via env, keeping logic expression-free.
3. Anti-rot test pins the wiring (canary workflow invokes scripts/canary_bridge.py subcommands; no logic-bearing run-blocks reappear beyond the allowlisted flush loop).
4. reconcile-bridge.yml is untouched except NO changes needed — its 13L exit-code case on "Run reconciler" is workflow-native annotation glue (::notice/::error) and stays.

## Scope
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml: 10 logic steps -> thin invocations (Check last successful run; Log canary result; Find/Open/Comment/Close heartbeat alert; Check binding-drift; Find/Open/Comment/Close drift alert). The flush loop and plumbing steps (mount, install, identity, signing key, seed, fail-on-stale) stay.
- scripts/canary_bridge.py: new module with the four subcommands.
- tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py: unit tests for classification + lifecycle transitions.
- tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py or a sibling anti-rot test: pin the canary wiring.
- tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py: RE-POINT — it asserts every `rebar transition ... closed` in the canary YAML carries --class (bug 0e15/ed13 guard); the close-on-recovery commands move to Python, so the guard becomes an assertion on scripts/canary_bridge.py's close calls (the protection survives, relocated).
- Verified-unaffected consumers (enumerated; assertions target steps that STAY): tests/interfaces/store/test_reconcile_workflow_no_shallow_rebase.py (parametrizes over reconcile-bridge-canary.yml; asserts fetch-depth:0 + merge-not-rebase invariants — the checkout/merge plumbing stays in YAML untouched); tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py (mount->init->first-merge ordering + no manual ours-driver — plumbing and flush stay in YAML), tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py (checkout `with:` inputs — checkout untouched), tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py (workflow `name:` — unchanged), tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py (bridge file untouched).
- pyproject.toml: T201 per-file-ignore for the new operational script — matching the LANDED legitimate-print entries (scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py, scripts/retarget_jira_project.py, scripts/check_server_manifest.py); f1eb's probe_rebar.py entry additionally lands before this via change 1275, stacked earlier in this epic.

## Testing
- Unit: classification matrix (api-error, never-succeeded, stale, fresh, malformed window input), each lifecycle transition (open-when-none, dedup-when-open, comment-when-still-stale, close-on-recovery, no-op paths), GITHUB_OUTPUT emission format, the rebar-error path (runner raises -> subcommand exits non-zero, loud), and a DRY_RUN=true case asserting ZERO rebar mutations. Runner seam injected (no live gh/rebar in unit tier).
- Anti-rot: workflow YAML parses; each replaced step invokes the module subcommand; flush loop still present verbatim (guard against accidental migration).
- Parity: trigger reconcile-bridge-canary.yml via workflow_dispatch in-session after merge; compare step outcomes/annotations to the last pre-migration scheduled run.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Canary logic steps reduced to env + single-command invocations; classification/lifecycle logic lives in scripts/canary_bridge.py with unit tests.
- [ ] Both CAS push loops (bridge commit-back, canary flush) remain in YAML byte-identical to pre-change; test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py still passes.
- [ ] Anti-rot test pins the canary wiring (invocations + no new logic-bearing run-blocks).
- [ ] tests/scripts suite green; lint/typecheck green.
- [ ] [operator-attested] One workflow_dispatch canary run post-merge shows parity (same stale/fresh classification and alert behavior as the preceding scheduled run); run id + outcome recorded in a ticket comment before close.

## File impact
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml (edit)
- scripts/canary_bridge.py (new)
- tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py (new)
- tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py (edit, or sibling anti-rot module)
- pyproject.toml (edit: T201 ignore)
